full_judgment:
6. We next consider the claim of tenancy right of the defendants in the suit lands. Though the defendants have claimed tenancy right in the lands of Schedules I and 2 since a long time before, we do not place any reliance upon such claim. They however, have exhibited documentary evidence, vie, Ext. F and Ext.C, Ekram name dated 7.7.1955 and pasta dated 26.7.56 respectively followed by rent receipts which would have created tenancy right of plaintiff-respondent in the lands if those had not been vitiated by absence of legal necessity. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondent has submitted that the Ekramnama Ext. F and patta Ext.C executed by sebait Tulshi Charaa on 7.7.1955 and 26.7.56 respectively were not for any legal necessity of the deity but was created collusively to defraud and deprive the deity of her properties, and as such these documents and dakhilas did not bind the deity. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondent has submitted that the defendants as transferees are to prove legal necessity and that the onus of proof of legal necessity is on the alienees. Mr. Khandoker, on the other hand, has submitted that since the averments in the plaint that there was no legal necessity for the alienation has not been asserted in trial Court, the purchaser has no duty to prove legal necessity. He has further submitted that no transfers had been made by Exts. F, C and the rent receipts granted by the Shebaits since these acts were done in ordinary course of management of the properties of the deity. Ext. F in an Ekramnama executed in favour of defendant No. 1 by Tulshi Baishnab dated 7.7.1955 covering the lands of 1st Schedule measuring 1 hal 1 kedar equivalent to 3.90 acre. The document is a base for 9 years of the lands at a fixed paddy rent of 18 palis valued at Tk. 100/- but there are other conditions in the said deed of Ekrarnama which are as follows: "If on the expiry of the stipulated period I resettle the said land with any other person in any Bummer, the same shall be rejected in law, and any amount of paddy or money paid without obtaining a receipt either from me or from a person appointed by me for the purpose, such payment should be disregarded". Similarly Ext. C is a patta dated 25.7.56 for a period of 9 years in favour of defendant No. 2 executed by Tulshi Baishnab covering the lands of Schedule 2 to the Plaint measuring 2 hals and 10 kedars. The stipulated rent fixed under the patta is Rs. 2/-per kedar. This patta also contains a provision as follows:" 

 On condition of payment of rent for the said land I hereby authorize you to enjoy and cultivate the said land. On the expiry of the stipulated period you will obtain a 2nd settlement in respect of the land mentioned in the schedule to this patta. In the alternative you will continue to cultivate the said land and make regular payments of the rent in terms of the patta. To this neither I nor my substitutes and successor shall have or can have any objection. If any objection is raised the same shall be rejected." The provisions of these two documents in our view have created permanent leases and cannot be said to be ordinary settlements of lands partaking the management of the affairs of the debuttor property. Besides these two documents namely, Ext F and C aforesaid, the appellants have alleged that the rent receipts granted by Tulshi Baishnab and Kamal Charan, the two shebaits of the deity, had created permanent tenancy rights with respect to the entire khan lands of the deity in favour of the recipients, The defendants have claimed permanent tenancy rights on the basis of the documents and the rent receipts with respect to the land of Schedules 1 and 2 and adverse possession for more than 12 years with respect to the lands of 3rd Schedule.
